name: Inductive Reasoning
definition: The ability to combine pieces of information to form general rules or conclusions (includes finding a relationship among seemingly unrelated events).

benchmark.name: ARC
benchmark.model_or_system: icecuber (Johan Sokrates Wind): brute-force program search over a hand-crafted DSL with 142 grid functions, composed in a DAG
benchmark.metric: percent of hidden private-test tasks solved (top-3 attempts allowed); equals 1 minus the official top-3 error of 0.794
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population. Inductive reasoning is a broad cognitive ability used across work settings. ARC was explicitly designed to need only core knowledge priors, not specialist training.

benchmark.name: ARC
benchmark.model_or_system: icecuber (Johan Sokrates Wind), a brute-force program search over a domain-specific language of 142 hand-crafted grid functions
benchmark.metric: percent of tasks solved on the hidden private test set (accuracy, up to 3 attempts per task)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population (typical adults doing novel few-shot rule induction)

benchmark.name: ARC
benchmark.model_or_system: icecuber (Johan Sokrates Wind) DSL brute-force program search, 1st place Kaggle Abstraction and Reasoning Challenge 2020
benchmark.metric: percent of hidden private test tasks solved (top-3 exact match; the Kaggle metric was the error rate, ~0.794, i.e. about 20.6% solved)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population. ARC requires only core-knowledge priors and no specialist training, so the typical working adult is the relevant population.

benchmark.name: ARC
benchmark.model_or_system: Team SM (Somayyeh Gholami & Mehran Kazeminia) and Team MindsAI (Jack Cole), tied for first place in ARCathon 2023
benchmark.metric: percent of private evaluation tasks solved exactly (task accuracy, ARCathon protocol with three attempts per task)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population (typical working adults doing novel few-shot rule induction; no specialist training is required for ARC)

benchmark.name: ARC-AGI
benchmark.metric: percent of tasks solved (accuracy) on the ARC-AGI-1 Semi-Private Evaluation set
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population (novel visual-grid inductive reasoning tasks require no domain expertise; the comparison is to typical crowdworker or educated adult solvers)

benchmark.name: ARC-AGI-2
benchmark.metric: percent of tasks solved (accuracy, pass@2) on ARC-AGI-2 Semi-Private Evaluation set
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population doing novel abstract rule-induction tasks. Inductive reasoning is a general cognitive ability used across occupations, so no specialist workforce applies.

benchmark.name: ARC-AGI-2
benchmark.metric: percent of tasks solved (accuracy) on the ARC-AGI-2 Semi-Private evaluation set
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population, the typical working adult applying inductive rule-finding from a few examples. Compared against ARC Prize's paid human calibration panel, which is likely somewhat more motivated and able than the median adult.
